children.text: The Stern-Gerlach experiment

Silver atoms of mass m=\(1.80\times10^{-25}\) kg leave an oven at T=1200 K with a common beam velocity along +z. Ignore gravity. They travel l1=0.25 m before an inhomogeneous magnetic region of length l2=0.50 m, then another l3=0.25 m to a screen. Each atom has moment ±μs x̂. For the field model two infinite insulated wires lie at (0,−a,z) and (0,+a,z), carrying −I0 ẑ and +I0 ẑ respectively in a medium of permeability μ=μ0μr. A narrow gap between two circles centred at C=(xc,0) and D=(xd,0), each passing through both wires, is replaced by low-pressure air. Assume its magnetic field is unchanged by removing the magnetic material. Along +x the right intersections of the C and D circles are R and Q, and P is the midpoint RQ. For numerical work use μr=\(10^{4}\),a=OC=0.60 cm,OD=0.80 cm,I0=2.00 A and μ0=\(4\pi\times10^{-7}\) SI. Use kB=\(1.381\times10^{-23}\) J/K.

children.text: The Stern-Gerlach experiment
a.1. Thermal beam speed
Equipartition gives mvz²/2=3kBT/2, so vz≈\(5.26\times10^{2}\) m/s.
b.1. Beam splitting

Transverse acceleration magnitude is μs|Gx|/m. Its deflection during the magnet and subsequent drift is \(\mu_s|G_x|[l_2^2/2+l_2l_3]/(mv_z^2)\). Two opposite moments double this: \[\Delta x=\frac{2\mu_s|G_x|l_2(l_2/2+l_3)}{mv_z^2}.\] The pre-magnet distance l1 has no effect.
c.1. Two-wire magnetic field

Superpose the two wire fields. Let \(D_\pm=x^2+(y\pm a)^2\). Then \[\mathbf B=\frac{\mu I_0a}{\pi D_+D_-}[(x^2-y^2+a^2)\hat x+2xy\hat y].\] This sign matches the stated upper +z and lower −z currents.
c.2. Field direction on a circular boundary

At R, y=0 and B points +x. At P0=(xc,√(xc²+a²)) the x component vanishes and the field points +y for xc>0. More generally on this right-hand circular arc the field is normal to the circle, as its cross product with (x−xc,y) vanishes.
c.3. Air-gap axial field
Set y=0 in C1: \(\mathbf B=\mu I_0a\hat x/[\pi(x^2+a^2)]\). The permeability in this model remains μ from the original magnetic circuit.
d.1. Dipole force magnitude

Differentiate Bx. For x>0 the gradient is negative, \(dB_x/dx=-2\mu I_0ax/[\pi(x^2+a^2)^2]\). The force magnitude is \(2\mu_s\mu I_0a|x|/[\pi(x^2+a^2)^2]\), with opposite signs for opposite moments. The field checks x>0.
e.1. Field and gradient at P
The right intersections are xR=xc+√(xc²+a²) and xQ=xd+√(xd²+a²). Thus xP=(xR+xQ)/2≈0.01624 m. Substitution gives B≈0.160 T and gradient magnitude ≈17.3 T/m. The signed gradient is negative.
f.1. Silver magnetic moment
Invert B1: \(\mu_s=m\Delta x\,v_z^2/[2|G_x|l_2(l_2/2+l_3)]\). With |Gx|≈17.34 T/m this gives μs≈\(1.04\times10^{-23}\) J/T.
g.1. Velocity-induced spot spread

Each spot displacement is xspot=Δx/2=0.10 cm and scales as vz⁻². Linear error propagation gives |δxspot|/xspot=2|δvz|/vz. Interpreting 20% as ±20% gives ±0.04 cm, hence positions from 0.06 to 0.14 cm in magnitude. If 20% is the full speed width, use ±10% and half this spot uncertainty. The source accepts both conventions.
h.1. Magnetic-moment uncertainty

Under the ±20% speed convention the inferred splitting uncertainty is ±40%, so \(\mu_s=(1.04\pm0.42)\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J/T}\). The full interval is approximately 0.62 to \(1.46\times10^{-23}\) J/T. A full-width 20% convention gives half that uncertainty. The source omits the factor \(10^{-23}\) in its final line, restored here.
